note: A laptop size of issue #114: it trains on one RTX 5080 Laptop GPU in about 480 minutes and gives a first sign of behavior; the maintainer reads its completions of the test prompts after each run. 13.7M parameters without the vocabulary's two tables, 30.5M with them (width 128, 21 layers: four window layers on each side of an exact layer, then two groups of one exact layer and five sparse layers), the balanced dataset's 65,536-token vocabulary and 32K-token windows. It reads the first 1,179,648,000 tokens of a corpus of 1,179,648,000, the size patient-tortoise reads, so one corpus serves the three laptop sizes: 3,000 updates of 12 windows, a warm-up of 120. The time assumes 45,550 tokens/s (measured on an RTX 5080 Laptop GPU with Triton kernels); `wpt train --stop-after-minutes` measures it. Its shape, learning rate and batch follow eldest-titmouse's laws at this width, but its tokens are set by the time, far below what the laws ask. Its 21 layers are the depth of the series #114 describes, of which it is meant to be the smallest size. Untested in a full run.
